title: Three-Zone Landscape Post-Processing Workflow in Photoshop and RAW (Sierra‑themed capture)

date.basis: embedded_creation_time from source metadata; filename suggests 2022 production

locations.name: Sierra Nevada (probable)
locations.basis: Source path contains 'Sierra'; transcript references mountainous terrain with snow, rocks and distant peaks; no explicit location named in speech

summary: The video presents a step-by-step landscape post-processing workflow focused on preserving sky detail, controlling dynamic range, and guiding the viewer’s eye toward the sun. The host emphasizes a non-destructive approach using Photoshop history states as if they were layers, straightens the image with perspective and puppet warps, and blends clouds to preserve a coherent sky. The workflow then expands into sky adjustments via RAW/Camera Raw with an HDR-like technique, introduces a dramatic “god beam,” and develops depth with a blur‑plus‑luminosity method for distant mountains, followed by tonal color grading and selective light painting to create a three-zone composition (sky, mountains, rocks). The tutorial stresses keeping highlights within a controlled range, building light direction, and iterating from large, global changes to smaller, nuanced refinements.

sections.title: Shot assessment and plan to straighten
sections.description: The shot is described as tilted about 10 degrees with a notable sun exposure balance. The host notes that the camera’s dynamic range is different from human vision and that exposure decisions should protect sky highlights before foreground detail. A plan to straighten the image is established as a prerequisite to further edits.

sections.title: Post-processing philosophy: flatten dynamic range and manage highlights
sections.description: The presenter outlines starting post-processing by lowering overall exposure to expand the apparent dynamic range, keeping foreground shadows usable and ensuring little to no sky highlights are blown out (within about one stop). He references camera contrasts (e.g., Nikon D850 vs Canon) and emphasizes avoiding excessive shadow noise by not underexposing the sky.

sections.title: Photoshop prep: history states and straightening
sections.description: Before edits, the workflow includes enabling a large history state count to treat each brush stroke as recordable history. This makes it possible to undo/redo adjustments as if they were layered edits.

sections.title: Perspective Warp workflow and trapezoid rule
sections.description: The image is straightened with perspective warp by dividing it into multiple boxes, then each box is warped to adjust perspective while preserving cloud detail. The host discusses the rule of trapezoids to produce a natural, wide-angle look and leading lines that guide the viewer toward the sun.

sections.title: Cloud handling and local adjustments during warp
sections.description: A cloud is cloned and reintroduced to preserve a strong leading line after the warp. The process uses selective blending and history brush-assisted edits to move and re-integrate cloud elements without introducing obvious artifacts.

sections.title: Sky elevation using RAW/Automatic HDR and beam creation
sections.description: The sky is processed using Camera Raw to create a dramatic beam of light. The host applies a three-pass application of an HDR-like adjustment (clarity, shadows, and noise reduction) to reveal hidden skies, discusses the artifact risk, and uses a history brush to disguise imperfections while preserving the beam.

sections.title: Blur + luminosity for depth and distance
sections.description: A blur plus luminosity technique is applied to distant mountains to soften them and create depth. The adjustments are painted selectively to emphasize far elements and light sources, with a global vignette-like effect to further draw the eye toward the sun.

sections.title: Color grading in RAW: tonal adjustments and highlight color
sections.description: The workflow includes RAW-based color strategies, such as tonal adjustments that selectively affect highlights, blues and camera calibration to render a gold tone on rocks, and targeted color grading in highlights to harmonize beams with the sky.

sections.title: Global refinement and final passes
sections.description: The image is darkened for a strong center focus, edges are vignetted, and a final warp/straightening check is performed to keep the composition cohesive. The host emphasizes big edits first, followed by refinements, to guide the viewer toward the source of light.

sections.title: Wrap-up and ancillary notes
sections.description: The session winds down with notes about transferring the shot from cards, a brief aside on focus stacking not being necessary for these landscapes, and commentary on the challenges of cloud conditions during that morning shoot.
